question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{3}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{3},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1+\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{10}-\sqrt{3}} & = \\ \frac{1+\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{10}-\sqrt{3}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{3}} & = \\ \frac{(1+\sqrt{6})(\sqrt{1}0+\sqrt{3})}{(\sqrt{10}-\sqrt{3})(\sqrt{1}0+\sqrt{3})} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{60}+\sqrt{18}}{(\sqrt{10})^{2}-(\sqrt{3})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{3}+2\sqrt{15}+3\sqrt{2}}{10-3} & = \\ \frac{3\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{10}+2\sqrt{15}}{7}\end{aligned}
$$
